spec.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeGroupAlias(created_at, '$__interval'),
  status AS metric,
  count(*) AS count
FROM
  message
WHERE
  $__timeFilter(created_at)
GROUP BY
  1,
  2
ORDER BY
  1

options.content: Cost over time (time series): the cost expression, summed per hour or day, split by model.
Cumulative cost (running sum): this shows burn rate against budget.
Cost per conversation (histogram plus a stat for avg and p95): compare it to conversation_max_cost (0.1). If many conversations sit near 0.1, the limit is hurting users or the prompts are too heavy.
Top 10 most expensive conversations (table): join conversation.description with the summed cost and turn count. Click through to inspect them.
Input vs output cost split (stat or pie): output tokens cost 5x more per token here (0.5 vs 0.1), so this shows whether output or input drives the bill.
Cost per message by status: failed messages that still burned tokens are pure waste.
Failure rate (%): count(*) filter (where status = 'Failed') / count(*). Add an alert on it.
Stuck messages (stat or table): status = 'In Progress' and created_at < now() - interval '5 minutes'. These are crashes or timeouts.

Tool iterations per message (histogram): if response or request_messages stores tool calls, extract the count with jsonb_array_length or jsonb_path_query. Compare it to the cap of 5 to see how often the agent hits the loop limit. Which JSON paths to use depends on how the app serializes messages, so check a real row first.

SELECT
  conversation_id,
  count(*)
FROM
  message
WHERE
  $__timeFilter(created_at)
GROUP BY
  conversation_id
ORDER BY
  1

options.content: Conversation duration (histogram): updated_at - created_at. The trigger keeps updated_at fresh on every message write, so this works as an engagement proxy.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT
  h.hour::text,
  d.dow::text,
  count(m.created_at) AS messages
FROM generate_series(0, 23) AS h(hour)
CROSS JOIN generate_series(1, 7) AS d(dow)
LEFT JOIN message m
  ON extract(hour FROM m.created_at) = h.hour
 AND extract(isodow FROM m.created_at) = d.dow
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 2

spec.description: Usage heatmap (hour of day vs weekday): extract(hour from created_at) and extract(dow from created_at). This shows when load peaks.
spec.title: Usage heatmap

SELECT
  $__timeGroupAlias(created_at, '$__interval'),
  SUM(COALESCE(input_tokens, 0)) AS "input tokens",
  SUM(COALESCE(output_tokens, 0)) AS "output tokens"
FROM
  message
WHERE
  $__timeFilter(created_at) 
GROUP BY
  1
ORDER BY
  1

spec.title: Input vs output tokens over time

spec.rawSql:
WITH numbered AS (
  SELECT
    row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY m.conversation_id ORDER BY m.created_at) AS turn,
    m.input_tokens
  FROM message AS m
  JOIN conversation AS c ON c.id = m.conversation_id
  WHERE m.status = 'Completed'
    AND $__timeFilter(c.created_at) 
)
SELECT
  turn,
  avg(input_tokens) AS "avg input tokens",
  (SELECT (value #>> '{}')::int
    FROM setting
    WHERE name = 'conversation_max_input_tokens' AND is_active) AS "limit"
FROM
  numbered
GROUP BY
  1
ORDER BY
  1

spec.description: Avg input tokens by turn number (line): use row_number() over (partition by conversation_id order by created_at) as the x axis. A steep curve means context growth is driving cost. Put the 20,000 limit (conversation_max_input_tokens) as a threshold line.
spec.title: Avg input tokens by turn number

spec.rawSql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(input_tokens, 0) as "input tokens",
  COALESCE(output_tokens, 0) as "output tokens"
FROM
  message
WHERE
  $__timeFilter(created_at)

spec.description: Token distribution per message (histogram or p50/p95/p99): this catches outliers near the 20k input and 4k output caps.
spec.title: Token distribution per message
